responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the Motorola/Freescale MCore architecture, covering the machine-specific parts of code generation from target option handling through RTL instruction selection to final assembly and object-format details. Its core configuration headers and backend implementation files define the MCore ABI, register set, calling and stack conventions, address and constant legality, frame layout, prologue/epilogue expansion, operand printing, symbol/section handling, cost and reorganization logic, and target hooks used during RTL expansion and emission; the machine-description, predicate, and constraint files supply the RTL patterns, operand classes, reload rules, scheduling and peephole behavior that map generic RTL onto concrete MCore instructions; and the option and ELF overlay files provide MCore-specific command-line controls plus ELF assembler/link conventions such as debugging, startup files, and import/export-related assembly behavior. Together these files distinguish the module as the architecture-specific lowering and assembly-emission layer for MCore, rather than a generic optimization or front-end subsystem.
